answer: Each identity joins the yarrow ledger, locks a 60-credit bond, and files three graded reviews from three ocean pools. Reviews form a spiral chain: clones on one funding root share a chain, so the kth clone re-checks earlier links at 20 plus 2 per prior link per review. A yarrow auditor grades reviews; a shallow or copied one burns 20, and three bad ones burn the bond. A rented-review ring fails because reviews are key-bound to assigned work and re-graded, so rented text scores zero. 1,000 clones pay 60,000 in bonds plus 3,057,000 in review work; an honest agent pays 120 and reclaims the bond.
